title: Human Reproduction
summary: Puberty, the male and female reproductive systems, the menstrual cycle, fertilisation and pregnancy, contraception and sexually transmitted infections.

notes.text: **Puberty** is the stage, usually between about 9 and 15 years of age, when the body becomes sexually mature and able to reproduce. It is triggered by **hormones**: mainly **testosterone** in boys and **oestrogen** in girls.

rows: Hair grows in the armpits and pubic area
Emotional changes and new interest in relationships

notes.caption: Male reproductive system
rows: Holds the testes outside the body, where it is cooler, so sperm develop properly
Carries sperm from the testes to the urethra
Add fluid to sperm to form semen
Deliver semen into the vagina; the urethra also carries urine

notes.caption: Female reproductive system
rows: Produce eggs (ova, the female gametes) and oestrogen
Carry the egg to the uterus; fertilisation takes place here
Where the baby develops; its thick lining supports the embryo
Ring of muscle at the opening of the uterus

notes.text: The **menstrual cycle** lasts about **28 days**. Each month the uterus lining thickens and an egg is released from an ovary (**ovulation**, around day 14). If the egg is not fertilised, the lining breaks down and leaves the body as blood through the vagina; this is **menstruation** (a period), lasting about 3 to 7 days.

items: During sexual intercourse, sperm are deposited in the vagina and swim through the uterus to the oviducts.
If a sperm meets an egg, the nuclei join: this is **fertilisation**, forming a **zygote**.
The zygote divides as it moves down the oviduct and becomes an **embryo**.
The embryo **implants** in the uterus lining (this is the start of pregnancy).
The **placenta** forms; through it oxygen and food pass from the mother's blood to the baby, and wastes pass back. The **umbilical cord** connects the baby to the placenta.
After about 8 weeks the embryo is called a **foetus**. Birth takes place after about **40 weeks** (9 months).

notes.label: Important
notes.text: Alcohol, smoking and drugs cross the placenta and can harm the baby. Drinking alcohol in pregnancy can cause **foetal alcohol syndrome**, which affects the child's brain and growth for life.

rows: Barrier that stops sperm from reaching the egg

notes.text: **Sexually transmitted infections (STIs)** are spread through sexual contact, for example HIV, syphilis, gonorrhoea and herpes. Many have no early symptoms, so testing is important; clinics give free, confidential help.
